title: React 19 Migration Prep
description: For the lead engineer scoping the React 18 to 19 / TypeScript 6 / .NET 10 upgrade. Walks through each blocker and improvement item with file-level evidence, ordered by priority.

steps.title: Migration scope — what's editable
steps.description:
## Migration Scope

This directory (`ClientApp/src/`) contains every file that needs to be assessed and potentially modified for the React 19 / TypeScript 6 migration.

**What this migration touches:**
1. React 18 → 19 API changes
2. TypeScript strict mode tightening for TS 6
3. New Design System component library replacing Bootstrap 5 + react-bootstrap
4. MSAL compatibility with React 19 (verify `@azure/msal-react` support)
5. React Router v6 → potential v7 upgrade

**What stays the same:**
- Business logic in route components
- Yup validators and custom string extensions (pure functions, no React)
- Session storage layer
- API client pattern (set token → call method)
- Authentication flow (B2C + MSAL)

**Priority order for this tour:**
1. **Hard blockers** — will throw at compile or runtime in React 19
2. **Compatibility reviews** — may work but need verification
3. **Quality improvements** — should be done during migration window

Navigate through each step in order — the migration checklist at the end consolidates everything.

steps.title: BLOCKER 1 — ErrorBoundary class component
BLOCKER 2 — React.Children.toArray in WizardForm
REVIEW — top-level await in index.tsx
steps.description:
**Priority**: 🟡 Review required

**Situation**: `await PublicClientApplication.createPublicClientApplication(configuration)` at the module's top level requires browser + bundler support for top-level await (TC39 proposal, Stage 4 in ES2022).

**Current status**: Works in Webpack 5 with `experiments: { topLevelAwait: true }` in the config, and in browsers that support ES2022 modules.

**React 19 consideration**: React 19 supports `<Suspense>` for async component rendering. The MSAL initialization could be restructured as a lazy-loaded async component instead of a blocking top-level await:
```tsx
// Alternative: lazy init inside a Suspense boundary
const App = () => (
    <Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>
        <MsalInitializer>
            <AccountProvider>...</AccountProvider>
        </MsalInitializer>
    </Suspense>
);
```
This would make the app's loading state more visible and testable.

**Gotcha**: If switching to React 19's `use()` hook for the async init, note that `use()` cannot be called conditionally — the component must consistently call it on every render.

steps.title: REVIEW — StrictMode double-invoke
steps.description:
**Priority**: 🟡 Review required

**Situation**: React 18/19 `<StrictMode>` invokes `useEffect` setup+cleanup+setup (twice) in development mode to surface effects with missing cleanup. React 19 makes this more aggressive.

**What to look for**: Effects that:
- Create subscriptions or event listeners without cleanup
- Fire analytics events (GA, App Insights) — these will double-fire in dev mode
- Create API calls without abort signal support
- Mutate external state (session storage, context)

**Known areas to check**:
- `Dashboard/index.tsx` — the large `useEffect` at line 343 must support abort signals and have a proper cleanup
- `AccountProvider.tsx` — any subscription setup must clean up
- `AppInsightsService.ts` — singleton init should guard against double-init

**Test approach**: Enable StrictMode in development, run through all 5 wizard flows and the dashboard, check the network tab for duplicate API calls and the App Insights log for duplicate events.

steps.title: REVIEW — MSAL React 19 compatibility
steps.description:
**Priority**: 🟡 Review required

**Situation**: `@azure/msal-react` wraps `@azure/msal-browser` with React hooks and context. MSAL React must be explicitly verified against the target React version.

**What to check**:
1. Is the installed version of `@azure/msal-react` declared as compatible with React 19 in its `peerDependencies`?
2. Does `MsalAuthenticationTemplate` use `React.Children` or deprecated Context APIs internally?
3. Does `useMsal()` work correctly under React 19's concurrent rendering and `<StrictMode>` double-invoke?

**Practical test**: Set up a test branch with React 19 RC and run the full auth flow:
- Sign in → verify token acquisition
- Session refresh → verify `acquireTokenSilent` works
- Sign out → verify `setActiveAccount(null)` + redirect
- MSAL cache + tab focus → verify no stale account state

**Fallback plan**: If `@azure/msal-react` is not React 19 compatible at migration time, consider wrapping the MSAL interaction in a React 18 compatibility layer (React 19 supports React 18 concurrent features), or use `@azure/msal-browser` directly without the React bindings.

steps.title: IMPROVE — any casts in env.ts for TypeScript 6
IMPROVE — Dashboard useEffect dependency array
steps.description:
**Priority**: ✅ COMPLETED

**Status**: Completed. `AbortController` cleanup and `useDebounce` (300ms) on the search text path have been added.

The Dashboard's data-loading `useEffect` now:
- Uses `AbortController` to cancel in-flight requests when the effect re-runs or the component unmounts
- Applies `useDebounce` at 300ms on the search text input so that keystrokes do not trigger an API call on every character

The `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` suppression has been addressed as part of this fix.

steps.title: Migration checklist
steps.description:
## React 19 / TypeScript 6 Migration Checklist

### 🔴 Hard Blockers (must fix before upgrading React)

- [x] **`ErrorBoundary` class component** → ✅ DONE — replaced with react-error-boundary functional boundary
  - Files: `components/ErrorBoundary/index.tsx`, update 3 usage sites
- [x] **`React.Children.toArray` in WizardForm** → ✅ DONE — replaced with React.Children.forEach accumulation
  - File: `components/forms/WizardForm/index.tsx:27`

### 🟡 Reviews Required (verify before upgrading)

- [ ] **Top-level `await` in `index.tsx`** → Verify Webpack 5 config supports it; consider migrating to Suspense-based init
- [ ] **`StrictMode` double-invoke** → Audit all `useEffect` hooks for missing cleanup; test for duplicate API calls
- [ ] **MSAL React 19 compatibility** → Check `@azure/msal-react` peer deps; run full auth flow on React 19 RC
- [ ] **React Router v6 → v7** → `RouteLeavingGuard` / `UnsavedFormPrompt` uses navigation blocking API that changed in v7

### 🟢 Improvements (do during migration window)

- [x] **`env.ts` `any` casts** → ✅ DONE — declare global + globalThis + startup guard
- [x] **Dashboard `useEffect`** → ✅ DONE — debounce + AbortController added
- [x] **`AccountContext` split** → ✅ DONE — AccountStateCtx / AccountDispatchCtx split implemented
- [x] **Modal flags in context** → ✅ DONE — ModalContext.tsx created, flags removed from AccountContext
- [ ] **Bootstrap 5 → Design System** → Replace `react-bootstrap` components across all routes and components; update SCSS theme

### 🔵 Post-Migration (after stable React 19)

- [ ] **`createHTML` TrustedTypes** → Implement DOMPurify sanitization for HTML injection vectors
- [ ] **Session storage keys** → Extract magic strings (`'accepted-quote-id'`, `'view-quote-id'`) to a `SessionKeys` enum
- [ ] **AppInsightsService null guard** → Add check before casting `ai.reactPlugin` as `ReactPlugin`
- [ ] **Phone regex normalisation** → Trim and normalise spacing before validation

### TypeScript 6 Specific

- [ ] Verify `declare module 'yup'` augmentation compiles under TS 6 strict settings
- [ ] Review all `any` casts for TS 6 propagation changes
- [ ] Check `FormikValues` generic constraints against TS 6's stricter object type inference
- [ ] Verify `web-api-client.ts` NSwag regeneration produces valid TS 6 code
